items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: I've made records with James P.

ctx.x: And Edmund Hall, Pete Brown and Cecil Scott, Don Frye, John Smith on guitar, Dick Fulbright--we talked about him earlier--you and Clarence Palmer the vocalist. And those were the ones for March 5th, 1937, and you did some ones on April 15th, a month later with Russell Procope and Slim Gaillard. Otherwise it was the same band. In 1939 it was Frankie, Mezz Mezzrow ... Pete Brown, James P.
Johnson, Al Casey, John Kirby and you. Do you remember those sessions at all?

items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: Of course as you see I've made records with James P.

ctx.x: Yeah, Corky Williams was another great pianist. Stride piano. He was there with Willie the Lion and Willie Gant, Corky Williams. Another one name of Price Jones. Dick Edwards.
I forgot to ask you yesterday when you were doing those rent parties, you were very young, did you run into Fats Waller and James P. Johnson at those?

Oh yeah, oh yeah. James P. Of course as you see I've made records with James P. I never made any, didn't make any records with Fats. But oh yeah, Fats Waller, they used to have those sessions, they used to be an after hour place there on 132nd Street and everybody used to go there and have those piano jam sessions and Willie the Lion Smith used to come in smoking his cigar, he was very braggadocious like, he'd just walk in you know and somebody's sit down there at the piano and he would walk in and everybody…
